title: Interface-Induced Modifications on the Atomic and Electronic Structures of La3Ni2O7
content: The recent discovery of superconductivity at approximately 80 K in the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) phase bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 under high-pressure conditions has led to extensive follow-on studies [1-5]. The RP nickelate phases are characterized by a layered perovskite structure, with n NiO2 layers interspersed between rock salt LaO layers. The occurrence of superconductivity in bilayer La3Ni2O7 is necessitated by both the extreme pressures involved and the desire to understand the intricate interactions between the different layers. In La3Ni2O7, the Ni ions possess an average 3d7.5 configuration, indicating partially occupied dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals. This unique electronic structure, coupled with strong electron correlations that give rise to superconducting pairing with both intralayer and interlayer characteristics [2–4], suggests a novel mechanism of superconductivity in this material.
